title: infrastructure-weekly-update-2026-09-07
body:
Summary:
This week focused on regional capacity balancing for upcoming Dedicated customer launches, continued onboarding of H100 nodes in us-west2, and a short incident related to NVLink firmware on a subset of A100 servers. We updated autoscaling profiles for busy model routes, ran cost vs. latency simulations for quantized vs. full-precision variants, and finalized PO paperwork for Q4 GPU purchases.

Highlights:
- Fleet expansion: 120 H100 nodes (80x H100 80GB + 40x H100 96GB) arrived at us-west2 and are in staging. Initial tests show a ~22% throughput improvement for long-context decoding workloads (seq=4096) vs. our latest A100 baseline.
- Regional capacity: us-west2 now has estimated available serving capacity of 2.6M tokens/min after staging; us-east1 remains our largest region at ~3.1M tokens/min. EU-west1 capacity held steady at ~1.4M tokens/min. We adjusted routing weights to send 12% more traffic to us-west2 for latency-sensitive routes.
- Incident: On 2026-09-05 we observed degraded inter-GPU NVLink performance on 6 A100 hosts in eu-west1 due to a firmware regression after a vendor update. Impact: transient 10-30% higher tail latency for multi-GPU batched workloads for ~3 hours. Mitigation: rolled back firmware on affected hosts, quarantined 6 hosts to maintenance label; post-mortem scheduled.
- Autoscaling and batching: deployed new autoscaler rules for Dedicated clusters that increase burst capacity thresholds by 15% for GPU pools serving chat routes. Enabled adaptive batching for short-turnaround routes which reduced per-token cost by ~8% in canary.
- Cost analysis: ran Q4 cost model with procurement team. H100 nodes reduce per-token GPU compute cost by estimated 12-18% for long-context heavy customers but increase fixed infra spend. Recommendation: prioritize H100 capacity for enterprise Dedicated pools and keep mixed A100/H100 pools for hosted API to preserve cost flexibility.
- Procurement: PO for 400 additional accelerators (mix of A100/H100) approved; delivery window estimated Oct–Nov 2026. Finance and legal sign-off complete.
- Private deployments: finalized network egress policy template for on-prem customers to simplify firewall configs. 

Metrics snapshot (end of week):
- Total GPU hosts (prod + staging): 2,480
- A100 hosts (prod): 1,420
- H100 hosts (prod + staging): 680 (staging: 120)
- Average serving utilization (prod): 64%
- 95th percentile token latency (hosted-api): 210ms
- Monthly committed Reserved Capacity (Dedicated): 18.5M token-minutes

Operational notes and work in progress:
1) NVLink firmware post-mortem (owner: Diego Martinez) — collect firmware versions, timeline, and vendor RCA. Target: 2026-09-10.
2) H100 runbook updates (owner: Sofia Patel) — add common troubleshooting steps, thermal thresholds, and kernel tuning knobs we discovered in staging. Target: 2026-09-14.
3) Autoscaler tuning for Dedicated (owner: Liam O'Connor) — observe new rules in prod canary for two weeks, roll to all Dedicated pools if error rate and latency remain within SLO. Target: monitor through 2026-09-21.
4) Capacity forecast Q4 (owner: Ava Chen) — finalize region-by-region capacity plan, include PO arrivals and estimated retirement of older A100 hosts. Draft due 2026-09-11.
5) Cost optimization eval (owner: eng-fin liasion) — simulate more aggressive prefix caching and larger KV cache for common prompt patterns; run A/B on top 10 Hosted routes. Target: 2026-09-18.

Risks and blockers:
- Delivery risk: vendor shipping delays could push H100 arrival into late-Nov and compress onboarding schedule. Contingency: extend burst contracts for Dedicated through cloud partners.
- Firmware drift: vendor-supplied firmware updates continue to be a vector for regressions; need a stricter validation gate in our staging pipeline. Proposed: automated NVLink perf tests in pre-prod for every firmware image.
- Capacity mismatch: growing EU demand may exceed eu-west1 capacity by mid-October if current growth trends continue. Short-term mitigation: temporarily route more EU traffic to us-west2 (with latency penalty) and prioritize Dedicated customers for EU-hosted capacity.

Requests / asks for other teams:
- SRE: please add NVLink firmware smoke test into pre-prod CI and alerting (contacts: Diego, Sofia).
- Procurement: confirm final delivery dates for the Oct/Nov PO and share serials when available.
- Product: provide list of top 5 latency-sensitive customer routes to prioritize H100 placement.

Notes and loose thoughts:
- Early H100 numbers are promising for long-context models; could enable new SLAs for enterprise customers that require <150ms median for seq <=1024 workloads if we colocate aggressively.
- We should track regional cold-start times separately for H100 vs A100 clusters — observed ~20% faster cold starts in staging for H100.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Diego: complete firmware post-mortem (due 2026-09-10)
- [ ] Sofia: update H100 runbook + add thermal thresholds (due 2026-09-14)
- [ ] Liam: monitor autoscaler canary and report (ongoing, initial check 2026-09-14)
- [ ] Ava: publish Q4 capacity forecast draft (due 2026-09-11)
- [ ] Procurement: confirm delivery schedule (ask by 2026-09-09)

Attachments / references:
- Confluence: GPU Fleet Runbook (linked above)
- Jira: ENGINFRA-4123 (NVLink firmware regression)
- PR: infra/pull/789 (autoscaler rule changes)

Next meeting:
Infrastructure weekly sync — 2026-09-09 10:00 PT. Agenda: firmware post-mortem, H100 staging results, Q4 capacity review, autoscaler canary status.
